name: Access and Mobility Management Function
summary: Terminates N1 (NAS) and N2 (NGAP): registration, connection and mobility management, reachability/paging, and NAS security. The 5G control-plane successor to the MME (minus session management).

name: Session Management Function
summary: Manages PDU sessions: UE IP address allocation, UPF selection and control over N4, QoS flow setup and charging interaction. Takes the session-management role split out of the EPC S/P-GW-C.

name: User Plane Function
summary: The 5G data-plane node: packet routing/forwarding, QoS enforcement, usage reporting and PDU session anchoring. Controlled by the SMF over N4 (CUPS). Combines the user-plane roles of the S-GW and P-GW.

name: Policy Control Function
summary: Provides policy rules (AM, SM and UE policy) to control-plane NFs and accesses subscription/policy data in the UDR. The 5G successor to the PCRF.

name: Unified Data Management
summary: Manages subscription data, authentication-credential generation (ARPF), user identification and serving-NF registration. The 5G front-end equivalent of the HSS, with data stored in the UDR.

name: Unified Data Repository
summary: Common storage back-end holding subscription data, policy data, structured exposure data and application data, accessed by the UDM, PCF and NEF.

name: Authentication Server Function
summary: Performs primary authentication of the UE (5G-AKA and EAP-AKA') on behalf of the AMF, working with the UDM/ARPF.

name: Network Repository Function
summary: Service registry of the SBA: NFs register their profiles and discover each other, and the NRF issues OAuth2 access tokens for NF-to-NF authorization.

name: Network Slice Selection Function
summary: Selects the set of network slice instances (NSSAI) and the target AMF set serving a UE.

name: Network Exposure Function
summary: Securely exposes 5GC capabilities and events (monitoring, QoS-on-demand, NIDD, device triggering) to external Application Functions. The 5G successor to the SCEF.

name: Application Function
summary: An application (operator or third-party) that influences traffic routing and policy, accessing the core directly (N5) or via the NEF.

name: Security Edge Protection Proxy
summary: Sits at the PLMN boundary and protects inter-operator (roaming) signalling over N32, applying message protection and topology hiding.

name: Service Communication Proxy
summary: Optional intermediary that provides indirect communication, routing and load balancing of service-based requests between NFs.

name: Network Data Analytics Function
summary: Collects data from NFs/OAM and provides analytics and ML-based insights (load, mobility, abnormal behaviour, QoS prediction) to consumers.

name: Charging Function
summary: Converged charging system for 5G: handles online (quota) and offline charging via the Nchf service, replacing the separate OCS/OFCS split.

name: Binding Support Function
summary: Stores and resolves the binding between a PDU session and the PCF serving it, so AFs/NEF can find the right PCF.

name: 5G Equipment Identity Register
summary: Checks the device identity (PEI/IMEI) status — allowed, blocked or monitored — over N17, the 5G analogue of the EIR.

name: Short Message Service Function
summary: Handles SMS over NAS for 5G subscribers, interworking with the legacy SMS infrastructure.

name: Unstructured Data Storage Function
summary: Optional shared storage where any NF can save and retrieve unstructured (opaque) state, enabling stateless NF designs.

name: Location Management Function
summary: Computes UE positioning in 5GS, coordinating measurements from the RAN and UE. The 5G counterpart of the E-SMLC.

name: Non-3GPP Interworking Function
summary: Connects untrusted non-3GPP access (e.g. WiFi) to the 5GC, terminating the UE IPsec tunnel and presenting N2/N3 toward the core. The 5G ePDG analogue.

name: gNodeB (5G NR base station)
summary: The 5G New Radio base station, connecting UEs to the 5GC over N2/N3. An ng-eNB is an LTE base station attached to the 5GC.

name: Mobility Management Entity
summary: The EPS control-plane node: attach/detach, EPS bearer and session management, paging, NAS security and authentication (with the HSS over S6a), and S-GW/P-GW selection.

name: Serving Gateway (S-GW)
summary: User-plane mobility anchor for intra-LTE and 2G/3G↔LTE handovers; routes/forwards packets and buffers downlink data for idle UEs.

name: PDN Gateway (P-GW)
summary: Anchor to external PDNs: UE IP allocation, policy enforcement (PCEF over Gx), online/offline charging and lawful intercept. Split into SMF + UPF in 5G.

name: Home Subscriber Server
summary: Master database of subscriber identities, service profiles and authentication data; serves the MME (S6a), IMS CSCFs (Cx), application servers (Sh) and AAA (SWx). Becomes UDM + UDR + AUSF in 5G.

name: Policy and Charging Rules Function
summary: Decides policy and charging control rules and pushes them to the PCEF over Gx; receives session/media info from AFs over Rx. The 5G successor is the PCF.

name: Online Charging System
summary: Performs real-time, credit-based charging and quota management over Gy/Ro; can interact with the PCRF over Sy for spending limits.

name: Offline Charging System
summary: Collects accounting records (CDRs) after the fact over Rf/Gz for post-processing and billing mediation.

name: Evolved Packet Data Gateway
summary: Secures access from untrusted non-3GPP networks (e.g. WiFi calling): terminates the UE IPsec tunnel (SWu) and connects to the P-GW over S2b. The 5G analogue is the N3IWF.

name: Equipment Identity Register
summary: Holds device identity (IMEI) status lists (white/grey/black) and answers MME/SGSN ME-Identity-Check requests over S13.

name: Service Capability Exposure Function
summary: Securely exposes EPC services to external service-capability servers / applications for cellular IoT: monitoring events, device triggering and Non-IP Data Delivery (T6a, S6t). The 5G successor is the NEF.

name: eNodeB (E-UTRAN base station)
summary: The LTE base station: radio resource management and the RAN endpoint of S1-MME (control) and S1-U (user) toward the EPC.

name: Serving GPRS Support Node
summary: Legacy 2G/3G packet-core control+user node; an S4-SGSN integrates with the EPC over S3/S4/S6d.

name: Gateway GPRS Support Node
summary: Legacy 2G/3G gateway to external PDNs over Gi; the functional ancestor of the P-GW.

name: Proxy Call Session Control Function
summary: The UE's first SIP contact point in IMS (Gm); enforces media policy via the PCRF/PCF (acting as the AF over Rx) for VoLTE/VoNR.

name: Serving Call Session Control Function
summary: The IMS registrar and central session controller: authenticates users, holds the registration, and invokes application servers via initial filter criteria (ISC).

name: Interrogating Call Session Control Function
summary: Entry point into a home IMS network: queries the HSS (Cx) to locate or assign the user's S-CSCF.

name: Access Session Border Controller
summary: Session border controller at the IMS access edge, between the subscriber's access network and the IMS core. Secures and adapts SIP signalling and RTP media for VoLTE/VoNR/VoWiFi: NAT/firewall traversal, topology hiding, SIP normalization and repair, media anchoring, transcoding, QoS marking and DoS protection. Realizes the 3GPP P-CSCF (IMS-ALG) plus IMS Access Gateway (IMS-AGW, controlled over Iq); acting as the P-CSCF it is the AF toward the PCRF/PCF over Rx.

name: Interconnection Session Border Controller
summary: Session border controller at the IMS network-to-network boundary (II-NNI), securing SIP signalling and RTP media exchanged with peer operators, IP interconnect and SIP trunks. Provides topology hiding (THIG), SIP protocol interworking and repair, transcoding, IPv4/IPv6 interworking, screening and admission control. Realizes the 3GPP IBCF (Interconnection Border Control Function, an IMS-ALG) plus Transition Gateway (TrGW, the media border controlled over Ix).

name: Telephony Application Server (MMTel AS)
summary: Hosts MMTel telephony services and supplementary services (call forwarding, barring, etc.) for VoLTE/VoNR; invoked by the S-CSCF over ISC and reads data over Sh.

name: Gateway Mobile Location Centre
summary: Entry point for location-services requests: queries the HSS (SLh) for the serving node and requests UE location from the MME (SLg).
